arxiv-2111-14447.title: ZeroCap: Zero-Shot Image-to-Text Generation for Visual-Semantic Arithmetic
arxiv-2111-14447.creator: Yoad Tewel, Yoav Shalev, Idan Schwartz, Lior Wolf
arxiv-2111-14447.description: Abstract Recent text-to-image matching models apply contrastive learning to large corpora of uncurated pairs of images and sentences. While such models can provide a powerful score for matching and subsequent zero-shot tasks, they are not capable of generating caption given an image.

arxiv-2305-01152.description: Abstract In this letter, we investigate rural large-scale path loss models based on the measurements in a central area of South Korea (rural area) in spring. In particular, we develop new close-in (CI) path loss models incorporating a diffraction component.

arxiv-2309-17335.title: Asynchronous Graph Generator Journal: Signal Processing
arxiv-2309-17335.creator: Christopher P. Ley, Felipe Tobar
arxiv-2309-17335.description: Abstract We introduce the asynchronous graph generator (AGG), a novel graph attention network for imputation and prediction of multi-channel time series. Free from recurrent components or assumptions about temporal/spatial regularity, AGG encodes measurements, timestamps and channel-specific features directly in the nodes via learnable embeddings.

arxiv-2310-18949.title: Customize StyleGAN with One Hand Sketch
arxiv-2310-18949.creator: Zhang Shaocong
arxiv-2310-18949.description: Abstract . Generating images from human sketches typically requires dedicated networks trained from scratch. In contrast, the emergence of the pre-trained Vision-Language models (e.g., CLIP) has propelled generative applications based on controlling the output imagery of existing StyleGAN models with text inputs or reference images. Parallelly, our work proposes a framework to control StyleGAN imagery with a single user sketch.

arxiv-2406-12592.creator: Shivank Garg shivank_g@mfs.iitr.ac.in, Manyana Tiwari m_tiwari@ma.iitr.ac.in
arxiv-2406-12592.description: Abstract In this paper, we extend the study of concept ablation within pre-trained models as introduced in ‘Ablating Concepts in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models’ by ( Kumari et al. 2022 ) . Our work focuses on reproducing the results achieved by the different variants of concept ablation proposed and validated through predefined metrics.

arxiv-2505-08597.title: Superconductor-Insulator transition in a two-orbital attractive Hubbard model with Hund’s exchange
arxiv-2505-08597.creator: Laura Torchia, Massimo Capone
arxiv-2505-08597.description: Abstract We study a two-orbital attractive Hubbard model with a repulsive Hund’s exchange coupling J J as an idealized model for a two-band superconductor. This framework is motivated by a system where a large isotropic electron-phonon coupling drives the on-site Hubbard repulsion U U negative, while leaving the exchange term unaffected.

arxiv-2511-21919.title: Identifying all snarls and superbubbles in linear-time, via a unified SPQR-tree framework
arxiv-2511-21919.creator: Francisco Sena, Aleksandr Politov ∗, Corentin Moumard, Manuel Cáceres, Sebastian Schmidt †, Juha Harviainen †, Alexandru I. Tomescu †
arxiv-2511-21919.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Francisco Sena, Aleksandr Politov ∗, Corentin Moumard, Manuel Cáceres, Sebastian Schmidt †, Juha Harviainen †, Alexandru I. Tomescu †. Snarls and superbubbles are fundamental pangenome decompositions capturing variant sites. These bubble-like structures underpin key tasks in computational pangenomics, including structural-variant genotyping, distance indexing, haplotype sampling, and variant annotation. Snarls can be quadratically-many in the size of the graph, and since their introduction in 2018 with the vg toolkit, there has been no published work on identifying all snarls in linear time.

arxiv-2512-03912.title: Parsimonious Clustering of Covariance Matrices
arxiv-2512-03912.creator: Yixi Xu 1, Yi Zhao 1
arxiv-2512-03912.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yixi Xu 1, Yi Zhao 1. Functional connectivity (FC) derived from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data offers vital insights for understanding brain function and neurological and psychiatric disorders. Unsupervised clustering methods are desired to group individuals based on shared features, facilitating clinical diagnosis. In this study, a parsimonious clustering model is proposed, which integrates the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) and covariance regression framework, to cluster individuals based on FC captured by data covariance matrices in resting-state fMRI studies.
